title: Non-decreasing Subsequences
statement: Return all distinct non-decreasing subsequences of length at least two.
explanation: Backtrack by appending values no smaller than the last chosen value and use a set at each recursion depth to avoid duplicate branches.

title: Target Sum
statement: Assign + or - signs to every number so the resulting sum equals target, and count the assignments.
explanation: Transform the signed sum into a subset-sum target and count subsets with that sum using DP.

title: Next Greater Element I
statement: For each value in nums1, find its next greater value to the right in nums2, or -1 if none exists.
explanation: Scan nums2 with a decreasing stack and map each popped value to the current greater value.

title: Diagonal Traverse
statement: Return matrix elements in diagonal zigzag order.
explanation: Walk diagonals and reverse direction at matrix boundaries.

title: Keyboard Row
statement: Return words that can be typed using letters from only one row of the American keyboard.
explanation: Map each letter to a keyboard row and keep words whose letters all belong to the same row.

title: Find Mode in Binary Search Tree
statement: Return all values that occur most frequently in a BST that may contain duplicate values.
explanation: Inorder traversal visits values in sorted order, allowing equal values to be counted in consecutive runs.

title: Next Greater Element II
statement: For each element in a circular array, find the next greater element or -1.
explanation: Scan the array twice and use a decreasing stack of unresolved indices.

title: Base 7
statement: Convert a signed integer to its base-7 representation.
explanation: Repeatedly divide the absolute value by seven and reverse the collected remainders, preserving the sign.

title: Relative Ranks
statement: Assign gold, silver, and bronze labels to the top three athletes and numeric ranks to the rest.
explanation: Sort original indices by descending score and write each rank label back at its original position.

title: Most Frequent Subtree Sum
statement: Return all subtree sums that occur most frequently.
explanation: Compute each subtree sum in postorder, count its frequency, then return sums with maximum frequency.
